rationale: Discussion of self‑labels and identity reinvention.
passage_text: THE REALITY OF LABELS: Novices say things like “I am tired” or “I am unlucky”. Nerfing their own reality with these labels. And you might think you’re smart.. You might use “empowering” labels, But here’s what most people fail to understand: Even empowering labels have weaknesses.. Think about it, “I am intelligent” Can make you avoid situations where you could look stupid. “I am spiritual” Can make you avoid ambition or material responsibility. “I am an entrepreneur” Can make you avoid work that feels operational. Understand: Labels have purpose. They can empower you, But they also narrow your identity, This limits you and puts an invisible cage around you. The key is this: Use labels when they strengthen you. But drop them the second they don’t serve you. Become Formless in an instant. And if you must keep only one label, let it be this: Learner. “I am a learner” has no limits. There is no cage. A learner is never finished. A learner assumes evolution. Wake up to reality.

The key is to reframe the situation from: “Annoying BS, Why me??” Reframe: This is a puzzle that has a solution. When I play chess, no matter how difficult of a position I am in, The game is still fun. if you ever played a challenging game, you know it’s kinda exciting. By gamifying my bank situation, I can’t wait to make my counter move. Overload them more documents than they asked for, Give them extra work to do. Write a professional letter with chatgpt which presents me as a lawyer. Cover all blindspots, give them headache And put them in check mate. Whenever you face problems, reframe it by gamifying it. passage_text: Boys, Bali has taught me a lot about spirituality, and it actually made me realize something crazy, which is some of the most quote-unquote spiritual people, like the people who claim to be on their spiritual journey, these people have some of the weakest spirits out there. I would never want them to have my back in a fight or in any form of challenge, because they'll whimper. I can't rely on them. They'll probably scurry away or start crying or whatever. and these are the people, like, they might attend ceremonies, they might meditate, talk about healing all the time, take psychedelics, and a lot of them, I'm going to be honest, bro, I've met a lot of them, a lot of them are quite arrogant, they feel enlightened, they feel like they know more than other people, because they went on this spiritual journey. I'll tell you what, bro, they have some of the weakest spirits. The only people that have weaker spirits than them are either people that give in to all their impulses, so give in to lust, give in to any form of overindulgence, or people that are complete NPCs in the slave system, in the rat system, that can't think for themselves, that are completely programmed, so they're completely disconnected from their own spirit, and they need to find it again. But other than those two groups, the NPCs and the people that give in to every impulse, other than those, these spiritual people are the next bottom tier, in terms of weak fucking spirit. And it's because they rarely challenge themselves physically. They think physical challenge is completely separate from spirituality. And it's like they don't understand, bro. Anything that truly tests your spirit is where you'll find the most spiritual growth. And so pain. Pain is where you'll find spiritual growth, bro. Fear. Like facing fear. Exhaustion. Doubt. But the most spiritual growth you'll ever experience is when something tries to break your spirit, but your spirit fights back and refuses to accept defeat.

DEALING WITH REGRET:

The best way to deal with regret is atonement.

People always say,

“Just let it go.”

But that’s bad advice.

If regret was meant to be immediately discarded,

it would serve no purpose.

Letting go comes after you’ve made up for it.

Make an oath to yourself.
Change the way you move forward.

Atone.

Then let go and forgive yourself.
